learning.models: Models untrusted data crossing an interpreter boundary.
learning.defense: Prefer parameterized APIs, allowlists and context-aware encoding.

learning.models: Models a request reaching an object or action outside the caller's authorization.
learning.defense: Enforce authorization on every protected request, deny by default and test object/function/field boundaries.

learning.models: Models repeated or distributed authentication abuse.
learning.defense: Use phishing-resistant MFA where appropriate, rate controls, risk signals and strong authentication telemetry.

learning.models: Models untrusted content reaching a browser execution context.
learning.defense: Use context-aware output encoding, safe framework defaults and a restrictive CSP.

learning.models: Models unexpected dependency or build artifact changes.
learning.defense: Pin and verify dependencies, review changes, generate provenance and gate artifacts before release.

learning.models: Models weak or missing protection around sensitive data.
learning.defense: Use modern authenticated encryption, protected key management and eliminate cleartext secrets.

learning.models: Models unsafe defaults and excessive exposure.
learning.defense: Harden defaults, remove unused services, minimize permissions and continuously verify configuration.

learning.models: Models unauthorized modification of data or artifacts.
learning.defense: Use integrity verification, signed/provenance-aware artifacts and immutable audit evidence.

learning.models: Models gaps or breaks in security telemetry.
learning.defense: Log security events consistently, protect logs from tampering and alert on material failures.

learning.models: Models failures that become security-impacting resource or control problems.
learning.defense: Fail safely, bound resources, handle timeouts and test degraded dependencies.

learning.models: Models cloud workload identity and network boundary failures.
learning.defense: Use workload identity, RBAC, network policy and secret management.

learning.models: Models suspicious endpoint process and file activity.
learning.defense: Use application/process controls, telemetry, isolation and evidence preservation.

learning.models: Models discovery of assets and services before an intrusion.
learning.defense: Maintain an authoritative asset inventory and minimize unnecessary exposure.

learning.models: Models an adversary crossing an initial trust boundary.
learning.defense: Reduce exposed surface, use strong authentication and validate every boundary.

learning.models: Models malicious or unexpected code/process execution.
learning.defense: Use application allowlisting, safe APIs, process controls and endpoint telemetry.

learning.models: Models unauthorized changes intended to survive normal lifecycle events.
learning.defense: Protect startup/configuration surfaces, require authorization and verify integrity.

learning.models: Models an unauthorized transition to higher privilege.
learning.defense: Apply least privilege, deny by default and monitor privilege changes.

learning.models: Models behavior designed to resemble normal activity or create telemetry gaps.
learning.defense: Correlate multiple signals and monitor telemetry continuity.

learning.models: Models tampering with defensive controls or sensors.
learning.defense: Protect security tooling, restrict administrative changes and alert on control changes.

learning.models: Models attempts to obtain or abuse authentication material.
learning.defense: Use MFA, credential hardening, secret isolation, rotation and anomaly detection.

learning.models: Models internal environment discovery after access.
learning.defense: Minimize information exposure, segment networks and monitor unusual enumeration.

learning.models: Models movement across trust boundaries.
learning.defense: Use segmentation, strong service authentication, least privilege and east-west monitoring.

learning.models: Models bulk or sensitive data access before exfiltration.
learning.defense: Enforce data access controls, minimize collection and alert on anomalous volume.

learning.models: Models unusual outbound control-channel behavior.
learning.defense: Restrict egress, use allowlists where practical and monitor traffic behavior.

learning.models: Models unauthorized transfer of sensitive data.
learning.defense: Restrict egress, monitor volume/destination and protect sensitive data.

learning.models: Models availability or integrity damage.
learning.defense: Use rate limits, isolation, backups, integrity controls and tested recovery.

learning.mechanism: Detects synthetic signals or techniques, then applies a bounded response action.
learning.limitation: A control only covers the signals and techniques mapped to it; combine layers and replay scenarios.
